This particular feature allows users to gain direct access to other main interfaces of PeaZip than file manager interface. In addition, it offers an overview of the objects that are displayed in file manager interface, which helps users to handle them better.
3.3.3 Functional Requirements

Users can use PeaZip for decompressing the contents of a selected (by them) compressed archive and extract them in a folder. Name and storage space of the folder in the computer system, are up to users to decide. The archive, whose contents are extracted, is neither destroyed, nor deleted and it is not left empty. On the contrary, it retains its content and name and remains saved at the same place of the computer system that was initially stored.
For the procedure of decompression and extraction to be completed, it is necessary that the selected archive is of one of the supported for extraction by PeaZip formats. In case the selected archive is encrypted,

user must know and insert password and (if there is one) keyfile in order to have access to the archives contents (for browsing or extracting them).
Read-only (browsing and extraction) formats supported by PeaZip: 7z, 7z-sfx, ARC/WRC, BZ2/TBZ2, custom, GZ/TGZ, PAQ/LPAQ, PEA, QUAD/BALZ, split, TAR, UPX, ZIP, ACE, ARJ, CAB, CHM, COMPOUND(MSI, DOC, XLS, PPT), CPIO, ISO, Java(JAR, EAR, WAR), Linux(DEB, PET/PUP, RPM, SLP), LHA/LZH, LZMA, Mac(DMG/HFS), NSIS, Open Office files, PAK/PK3/PK4, RAR,SMZIP, U3P, UDF, VHD, WIM, XAR, XPI, XZ, Z/TZ

Browse most recently visited item - F7

Open directory/archive - < or Enter or double click on the folder/archive   
Up one level - > or Ctrl+U or click on blue arrow icon or F4

Forward in history - Ctrl+F
Extract:
Extract all content - Ctrl+A   
Extract displayed content - Ctrl+D   
Extract selected content - Ctrl+S

Extract selected - Ctrl+Enter

Note: "extract selected" extracts the entire selected archive(s) if browsing the file system, and selected object(s) if browsing an archive.

Extraction (this feature is described in previous chapters)of the content of encrypted(locked) archives through PeaZip, shouldn’t be allowed without inserting the correct password and (if existing) keyfile for authentication. Finally, no data remains from data that have been selected to be securely deleted should be left in the storing area of the computer system after the end of the procedure of secure deletion (described in previous chapter), in case of selection of this feature.

Appendix B: Analysis Model
The diagram illustrates a system architecture centered around the “File Manager Interface,” which serves as the primary hub connecting multiple components and user interactions.

At the top center, the “User” interacts directly with three main interfaces: the “File Manager Interface,” the “Extract Interface,” and the “Create Archive Interface.” The “User” also connects to the “Settings Interface” via the “File Manager Interface.”

On the left side, four functional modules feed into the “File Manager Interface”:
- “Browsing Computer System’s Locations”
- “Object Selection/View Mode Alternation”
- “Computer System Management Tools”
- “File Management Utilities”

Additionally,

the “File Manager Interface” connects bidirectionally with the “Settings Interface” and receives input from “Password and Keyfile Use,” which also links to both the “Extract Interface” and the “Create Archive Interface.”

On the right side, the “Extract Interface” and “Create Archive Interface” are interconnected. Both receive input from the “Drag and Drop Feature,” which also points to the “Graphic display of currently executed functions.” This graphic display module further feeds back into both the “Extract Interface” and the “Create Archive Interface,” and also connects to the “File Manager Interface.”

All connections are represented by directed arrows indicating flow or dependency relationships between components. No numerical values or additional metadata are present in the diagram.
